drivers.driver: The Company is a conglomerate with a significant sum-of-the-parts discount created by the market's inability to value the core advertising business separately from its Asian affiliate stakes [D01], [D04].
The removal of the CEO on September 6, 2011, and the commencement of a strategic review provide the necessary catalyst to force management to unlock value [D02], [D03].
We intend to act as a constructivist shareholder to ensure the board prioritizes a tax-efficient separation of assets rather than status quo management or value-destructive acquisitions [D02], [D03].
The annual meeting process provides a clear governance route to enforce board accountability and secure representation if the strategic review fails to deliver [D03].

final.memo:
The Company is an iconic, yet chronically mismanaged, internet conglomerate. While it possesses a massive, broad-reaching audience across its core advertising platforms, the market has persistently penalized the stock, assigning it a significant discount due to the murky combination of these operating assets with its valuable, high-growth Asian affiliate stakes [D01], [D04].

When viewed on a sum-of-the-parts basis, the current market valuation fails to reflect the intrinsic worth of the Asian interests [D01]. Benchmarked against pure-play internet and media peers, it is evident that the market is mispricing the core advertising business and failing to credit the company for its stakes in these highly liquid and separable assets [D01], [D04].

The market’s pessimism is rooted in historical board inertia and a fear that management will attempt to 'fix' the company through inefficient, value-destructive acquisitions rather than focusing on shareholder returns [D04]. Our view is that this conglomerate discount is entirely reversible through a disciplined, tax-efficient separation of the Asian assets [D01].

The board’s decision to remove the CEO on September 6, 2011, and initiate a strategic review, is a necessary first step [D02]. We intend to engage proactively to ensure this process is not merely a bureaucratic exercise. We demand a clear timeline for the CEO search, board refreshment with qualified internet and media experts, and a commitment to monetize the Asian affiliates [D02], [D03]. We are prepared to utilize the upcoming annual meeting process to hold directors accountable for these objectives [D03].

Risks include the potential for management to pursue ill-advised 'transformational' strategies during the review period [D04]. However, our thesis provides a clear floor based on the realizable value of the Asian assets, protecting our downside [D01]. Should the board abandon the path to separation, our thesis will be considered broken, and we will exit our position immediately [D04].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock. This sizing reflects our conviction in the strategic review process, tempered by the necessity of waiting for further liquidity and financial clarity as the review matures [D04], [D05]. We will hedge our market exposure using S&P 500 index puts to mitigate volatility during this period of restructuring [D04].
